headline: Spain extends winning streak with 3-1 victory over Czech Republic in Nations League
summary: Spain secured their third consecutive win in the UEFA Nations League, maintaining their top spot in Group A3. Lamine Yamal, Rodri, and Mikel Merino scored for Spain.
details: World champions Spain defeated the Czech Republic 3-1 in the UEFA Nations League, extending their winning streak. The victory, secured on Saturday (October 3) at their home ground in Oviedo, also maintained Luis de la Fuente's team's top position in Group A3.
Spain took an early lead in the sixth minute. Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal skillfully sent the ball into the far post with a curling shot from outside the box, navigating through three defenders.

The lead was doubled in the 35th minute by former Manchester City midfielder Rodri. The Barcelona midfielder exchanged passes with Dani Olmo before firing a powerful shot into the top corner from near the penalty spot.

Jiří Sláma reduced the deficit for the Czech Republic in the 69th minute, beating Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya with a low shot. However, the Czech Republic was reduced to 10 men late in the game when Wolves defender Ladislav Krejčí received two yellow cards and was sent off.

Mikel Merino, an Arsenal midfielder, sealed Spain's victory with a goal in the 89th minute. This win marks Spain's tenth consecutive victory, having remained unbeaten since a goalless draw against Cape Verde in the World Cup group stage.

Spain now has 9 points from three Nations League matches, leading Group A3 by three points ahead of second-placed England, who thrashed Croatia 7-0 on the same day. Spain will face Croatia next on Tuesday, where a win would secure their quarter-final spot with two group stage matches remaining.
Spain recently won the 2026 World Cup final, defeating Argentina 1-0. They also secured the Nations League title in 2023, though they were runners-up in the 2021 and 2025 editions.

headline: Lula's lead over Bolsonaro narrows ahead of Brazil's first-round vote
summary: A new poll shows a tighter race between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, indicating a potentially close runoff election.
details: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's lead over Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has narrowed significantly ahead of Sunday's first-round vote, according to a recent CNT/MDA poll. The survey also suggests a much tighter contest in a potential runoff election.

In the first-round scenario, Lula is projected to receive 43.1% of voter support, while Bolsonaro follows with 38%. Other candidates like Augusto Cury (3.2%), Ronaldo Caiado (3%), and Renan Santos (1.5%) trail behind.

This marks a shift from a Sept 15 poll, where Lula held 40.5% and Bolsonaro 30.4%, indicating a substantial gain for Bolsonaro. When considering only valid votes, Lula's support stands at 47.8% against Bolsonaro's 42.1%.

If no candidate secures over 50% of valid votes in the first round, the top two contenders will proceed to a runoff election on October 25. The poll projects Lula would receive 47.3% in a runoff, compared to 43.1% for Bolsonaro.

The previous survey showed Lula leading Senator Bolsonaro by 47.3% to 40% in a runoff scenario, suggesting the gap has also closed in a potential second round. The CNT/MDA poll surveyed 2,007 people from Sept 30 to Oct 2, with a margin of error of 2.2 percentage points.
